title: Trace Needle: rapid search & correlation flow for request traces
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a focused, search-first trace exploration flow (nicknamed 'Trace Needle') that helps engineers find the single request or span of interest inside long traces and quickly see correlated metadata (logs, customer id, headers, downstream spans). This is intended as a complementary, fast-path alternative to the full trace waterfall UI for investigation workflows.
context: Current console trace views are waterfall-first and optimized for visual correlation and timeline analysis. Support tickets and user interviews show people frequently need a quick way to 'needle' into a trace with a correlation id, error signature, or short regex and jump to the exact moments, with supporting context (logs, sampling info, routing policy). We must preserve existing deep-dive capabilities while offering a faster investigative entrypoint.
problem_statement: Engineers spend too long scanning long waterfalls to locate the span(s) that match a correlation ID, error pattern, or API path; we need a fast, memory-efficient search + focused timeline view that surfaces relevant spans and surrounding context.
goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-insight for trace investigations by 50% for median cases.
- Surface the correlation ID and propagated headers prominently.
- Allow fast pivoting from search result to full waterfall or request replay.
- Keep the feature performant on traces >500 spans and in browser-limited environments.
proposal_overview:
Flow summary:
1) Top-level Query Bar: free-text + structured tokens (correlation_id:, service:, status:, latency>, path:, regex:). Autosuggest based on recent queries.
2) Result Needle List: compact list of matching spans across the trace with inline key metadata (timestamp, duration, service, status code, snippet of message). Each row shows a small sparkline of local timeline.
3) Focused Timeline Pane: selecting a needle opens a centered timeline that zooms to the span with ± configurable context (default 500ms before/after). Keyframes (child spans crossing service boundaries) are highlighted.
4) Sidecar: pinned context panel with raw headers, log lines with links to log viewer, request payload, and links to relevant APM traces or deployment metadata.
5) Quick Actions: open full waterfall (preserves zoom), create incident note with snapshot, deep-link share, and open in Request Replay studio.
6) Filters/Facets bar: one-click chips (error, slow, sampled, un-sampled, model-serving) and time bucketing to refine results.
7) Accessibility: keyboard-first operations (press / to focus search, j/k to navigate results, enter to open sidecar).
design_notes:
Decisions so far:
- Use compact row list rather than full waterfall for initial results to improve scan-speed and memory usage.
- Color palette reuses existing service color tokens; error statuses get a saturated accent to surface quickly.
- Timeline uses continuous scale with an overlay to show selected span context; we will lazy-render waveform/sparklines to avoid jank on large traces.
- Prefetch minimal sibling spans and logs when a needle result is hovered to make sidecar open feel instantaneous.
- Deep-link format: /console/traces/<trace_id>?needle=<span_id>&zoom=ms to support sharing and support for Dedicated/Private URL schemes.
- Mobile: fallback to a single-column list with CTA to open full trace on desktop.
edge_cases:
- Extremely large traces (>2000 spans): cap initial results to first 500 matches and show progressive load.
- Missing correlation ids: allow fuzzy UI search against attributes (http.path, user.id, request-id).
- Collapsed merged spans: show a 'merged count' affordance with option to expand to constituent spans.
- Sampled vs unsampled: surface sampling rate and link to sample bias docs.
- Partial traces across regions/zones: surface origin region and time sync offset note.
acceptance_criteria:
- Query bar supports structured tokens and returns results in <500ms for traces up to 1000 spans in local dev env.
- Selecting a needle opens focused timeline with sidecar populated and at least 3 lines of logs when available.
- Quick action 'Open full waterfall' preserves zoom center and highlights the selected span.
- Deep-link opens the Trace Needle view and focuses the selected span.
- Design review sign-off from PM, Eng (serving runtime), and SRE is recorded.
- Prototype available in Figma + interactive prototype link and included in design handoff.
feedback_and_reviews:
Design review notes (2026-02-18):
- PM (Noah Reed): clarify how query suggestions are seeded from console usage and recent queries.
- Eng (Sanjay Iyer): confirmed lazy-render approach for sparklines; requested memory profiling in prototype.
- SRE (Maya Thompson): asked for explicit sampling metadata and 'trace completeness' indicator.
- Accessibility (Lina Gomez): requested focus states and ARIA labels for needle list rows.
Follow-ups: add telemetry events for needle_open, needle_result_click, needle_share. Prototype pushed for usability testing 2026-02-25.
outstanding_risks:
- Memory/performance regressions on large traces if sparklines are not sufficiently lazy-rendered.
- Misleading results if semantic tokenization of headers (eg corelation id variants) is incomplete.
- Potential UX confusion between needle-focused timeline and full waterfall; must keep clear affordance to switch.
handoff_notes:
- Export tokens and CSS variables for timeline colors.
- Provide a list of telemetry events and schema for instrumentation.
- Include a small sample dataset (capped 800 spans) to use for QA perf testing.
- Add unit visual spec for needle row states: default, hover, focused, pinned, error-highlight.
